classification.difficultyReason: Apply the taught repayment derivation to two fully specified mortgages, then use rounded repayments to compare totals.

content.prompt: Get Rich Bank offers a mortgage at $7\frac12\%$ p.a. over 10 years and Capital Bank offers a mortgage at $5\frac12\%$ p.a. over 25 years, both with interest calculated monthly.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the amount of the monthly repayments for each bank on a loan of $\$80\,000$. Give your answers to the nearest cent.

answer.short: Get Rich Bank: $\$949.61$ per month. Capital Bank: $\$491.27$ per month.
answer.worked:
Let $M$ be the monthly repayment.

Get Rich Bank:
$$\begin{aligned}r&=1+\frac{0.075}{12}=1.00625\\n&=10\times12=120\end{aligned}$$
Start: $80\,000$.

After the first repayment: $80\,000r-M$.

After the second repayment: $80\,000r^2-Mr-M$.

After the 120th repayment: $80\,000r^{120}-Mr^{119}-\cdots-M$.

The repayment terms form a geometric series with first term $M$, common ratio $r$ and 120 terms. When the loan is repaid, the balance is zero.
$$\begin{aligned}0&=80\,000r^{120}-M\frac{r^{120}-1}{r-1}\\M&=\frac{80\,000r^{120}(r-1)}{r^{120}-1}\\M&\approx\$949.61\end{aligned}$$
Capital Bank:
$$\begin{aligned}r&=1+\frac{0.055}{12}\\n&=25\times12=300\end{aligned}$$
After the 300th repayment: $80\,000r^{300}-Mr^{299}-\cdots-M$.

The repayment terms form a geometric series with first term $M$, common ratio $r$ and 300 terms.
$$\begin{aligned}0&=80\,000r^{300}-M\frac{r^{300}-1}{r-1}\\M&=\frac{80\,000r^{300}(r-1)}{r^{300}-1}\\M&\approx\$491.27\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the difference in the total amount paid on each mortgage. Use the rounded repayments from part (a).

answer.worked:
Using the rounded repayments from part (a):

Get Rich Bank total:
$$120(949.61)=\$113\,953.20$$
Capital Bank total:
$$300(491.27)=\$147\,381.00$$
Difference:
$$147\,381.00-113\,953.20=\$33\,427.80$$
Therefore Capital Bank costs $\$33\,427.80$ more.
